taskVersion.name: ves-real-item

parts.text:
Curve-type notation for vertical electrical sounding (VES): take the layer resistivities in depth order. For each group of three consecutive layers (layers 1-2-3, then 2-3-4, and so on), write one letter: A if r1 < r2 < r3; Q if r1 > r2 > r3; H if r1 > r2 < r3; K if r1 < r2 > r3. A curve with N layers gets N-2 letters, in depth order (for example, a 4-layer curve gets 2 letters, such as HA). If all the letters are the same, the curve may also be written as that single letter (AAA may be written A).

Station Choba-LawnTennisField, Lawn Tennis Field, University of Port Harcourt, Choba Town. Interpreted layer model:

Layer | Resistivity (ohm-m) | Thickness (m) | Depth to base (m)
----- | ------------------- | ------------- | -----------------
1 | 91.2 | 2.535 | 2.535
2 | 380.2 | 15.83 | 18.37
3 | 43.25 | 20.36 | 38.73
4 | 474.3 | 33.05 | 71.78
5 | 597.1 | - | -

The survey interpretation on file classifies this station's curve as KHA-type.

Is this label correct for these layer values? Give a short answer, then end with one JSON line exactly like this:
{"label_correct": true or false, "curve_type": "<letters>"}

To determine the curve-type notation, we examine each group of three consecutive layers based on the provided resistivity values: $\rho_1=91.2$, $\rho_2=380.2$, $\rho_3=43.25$, $\rho_4=474.3$, and $\rho_5=597.1$.

1.  **Layers 1-2-3**: $91.2 < 380.2 > 43.25$. This follows the pattern $\rho_1 < \rho_2 > \rho_3$, which is **K**.
2.  **Layers 2-3-4**: $380.2 > 43.25 < 474.3$. This follows the pattern $\rho_2 > \rho_3 < \rho_4$, which is **H**.
3.  **Layers 3-4-5**: $43.25 < 474.3 < 597.1$. This follows the pattern $\rho_3 < \rho_4 < \rho_5$, which is **A**.

Combining these gives the sequence **KHA**.

{"label_correct": true, "curve_type": "KHA"}
